summary: The University of Gothenburg awards the Axel Adler Scholarship to fee-paying students on its international programmes. It waives the tuition fee for the whole of a full-time master's or one of seven bachelor's programmes, with one scholarship for each master's and each eligible bachelor's programme.
meta_title: Axel Adler Scholarship 2027: University of Gothenburg tuition waiver
meta_description: The Axel Adler Scholarship waives tuition for a whole University of Gothenburg programme. Apply by 15 January 2027, then 10 February to 8 March.
covers: The tuition fee for your whole programme: four semesters for most master's, two for a one-year master's and six for a bachelor's.
FAS+ insurance while you hold the scholarship.
Living and accommodation costs are not included.
eligibility: You must be required to pay tuition fees in Sweden: in general, citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. You do not need to have paid the fee before applying.

You must apply for an international campus-based programme at the University of Gothenburg and rank it first on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027. If you apply to several Gothenburg programmes, only your first choice counts.

To be awarded it you must be admitted to a full-time master's or to one of these full-time bachelor's programmes: Software Engineering and Management, Computer Science and AI, International Relations, Business and Economics, or the BFA programmes in Metal Art, Wood Oriented Furniture Design and Craft (Crafting Futures).
how_to_apply: Apply for your programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027, with the University of Gothenburg as your first choice.
Pay the application fee and upload the documents showing you meet the entry requirements by 1 February 2027.
Eligible applicants get an email with an invitation to apply around 10 February 2027. Check your spam folder if it does not arrive.
Write your CV and letter of motivation in the scholarship application system and submit by 8 March 2027. You cannot attach documents.
Results come by email on 12 April 2027 for master's applicants and 15 April 2027 for bachelor's applicants.
watch_out: You must be admitted as well as selected, and only your first-choice programme counts.
Sweden's residence permit asks you to show money to support yourself, and the scholarship does not pay living costs.
If your permit does not come in time to start your programme, the scholarship is withdrawn, and a late permit is not a valid reason for deferring.
To keep the scholarship you must complete at least 75% of the credits each semester.
costs: Tuition fee for your whole programme
The scholarship, in full, if you win it
You, when you apply on universityadmissions.se
Living and accommodation costs in Gothenburg
You; the scholarship does not cover them
You; apply as soon as you are awarded the scholarship
documents: Your universityadmissions.se application, with the University of Gothenburg first and the application fee paid by 1 February 2027.
The documents showing you meet the programme's entry requirements, uploaded by 1 February 2027.
A CV and letter of motivation, written in the scholarship application system between 10 February and 8 March 2027.

faq.q: Does the Axel Adler Scholarship cover living costs?
faq.a: No. It waives the tuition fee for your whole programme, and you pay your own living and accommodation costs. It does include FAS+ insurance.

faq.q: When can I apply for the Axel Adler Scholarship for 2027?
faq.a: Apply for your programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and send your documents by 1 February. Eligible applicants are then invited by email around 10 February and apply for the scholarship by 8 March 2027.

One for each master's programme and each eligible bachelor's programme, with four in all across the Artistic Faculty's programmes. Up to ten more may go to the programmes with the most applicants if funds allow.

faq.q: What is the Axel Adler Scholarship for Sustainability?
faq.a: An extra tuition waiver for students admitted to the university's sustainability-focused master's programmes, with 2 to 12 awarded. You apply for it in the same application if you are eligible for both.
